name: blockif_open
prose: Opens a block backing file described by the nvlist nvl and returns a new context, or NULL (usr.sbin/bhyve/block_if.c:476-677; slice cut the head). It runs blockif_init once, reads the booleans nocache (O_DIRECT), nodelete, sync/direct (O_SYNC) and ro, an optional 'sectorsize' ('N' or 'N/M' via strtol; a bad string goes to err), and an optional 'bootindex' (atoi). A missing 'path' goes to err. It opens the file read-write (or read-only with ro), and if the read-write open fails retries read-only and sets ro; an open failure (warn) or fstat failure goes to err. With Capsicum it limits the descriptor rights (rights failure: errx(EX_OSERR)). For a character device it fetches the media size and sector size with ioctl (failure: perror and err), asserts both are non-zero, and reads the optional stripe size and offset, the GEOM candelete attribute (unless nodelete) and the provider name with ioctls whose failures are ignored; for other files the physical sector size is st_blksize and candelete comes from fpathconf. With Capsicum it limits the ioctl set (failure: errx(EX_OSERR)). If a sector size was given it must be a power of two with 512 <= ssopt <= pssopt and pssopt a power of two (else err), and for a character device ssopt must be at least the device sector size and a multiple of it (else err); the given sizes then replace the detected ones. It callocs a blockif_ctxt (perror and err on failure), fills in the fields (magic BLOCKIF_SIG, fd, ischr, isgeom, candelete, rdonly, size, sector sizes, bootindex), initialises its mutex and condition variables and the three request queues with all BLOCKIF_MAXREQ requests on the free queue, creates BLOCKIF_NUMTHR worker threads named blk-<ident>-<i> (pthread_create results are not checked), and returns the context. On every err path it closes the descriptor if one was opened and returns NULL. The returned context owns the descriptor and must be released with blockif_close.

prose: Registers an event with the bhyve mevent loop (usr.sbin/bhyve/mevent.c:283-356). If tfd < 0 or func is NULL it returns NULL immediately, before running mevent_init (via pthread_once) and before taking the queue lock. Otherwise it calls pthread_once(mevent_init), takes the queue lock and rejects (jumps to exit and returns NULL) a duplicate: for a type other than EVF_TIMER, an entry with the same me_fd and type already on global_head or change_head; timers are not checked for duplicates. It callocs a struct mevent (NULL on failure), stores for a timer me_msecs = tfd and a new me_timid, otherwise me_fd = tfd, and records type, func, param, state and fflags. It builds a kevent with mevent_populate and registers it synchronously with kevent(mfd, ...); on failure it frees the new struct and returns NULL. On success it clears EV_ADD from me_state (other bits such as EV_DISABLE are kept), inserts the entry at the head of global_head and returns it. The queue lock is held from after the first two returns to exit (released at exit on every path that took it).

name: rfb_send_screen
prose: Sends the changed parts of the framebuffer to the VNC client on cfd (usr.sbin/bhyve/rfb.c:691-871). It first tries to set rc->sending from false to true atomically; if another thread already holds it, it returns 1 without touching any state (the sending flag is not cleared by this call). Once it owns the flag, every later path leaves through done, which sets rc->sending = false and returns retval (initially 1). It atomically clears rc->pending and, if it was already false, goes to done with 1. If update_pixfmt was set it recomputes the pixel adjustment, refreshes the console and takes the console image, and resets the CRC cache when the image size changed. If the size differs from the client's size it stores the new size and, when enc_resize_ok is set, sends a resize message: a negative result makes it return -1, otherwise it sets update_all and returns 1. If update_all was set it clears it and returns the result of rfb_send_all. Otherwise it computes CRC32 per 32x32 cell and marks the cells that changed; if none changed it sets rc->pending back to true and returns 1; if the changed percentage is at least RFB_SEND_ALL_THRESH it returns rfb_send_all(...); else it writes an update header (a result <= 0 returns -1) and sends each changed cell with rfb_send_rect, returning nwrite as soon as one returns <= 0 (so 0 or a negative value, not necessarily -1), and returning 1 when all cells were sent. The values returned by rfb_send_all and rfb_send_rect (not read) are passed through.

name: kbd_process_keys
prose: Compares the keys in the current HID report (s->keys1) with the keys pressed before (s->keys2) and emits release and press events (usr.sbin/bluetooth/bthidd/kbd.c:339-413; s->vkbd and s->ukbd are file descriptors). It always returns 0. It finds the first set bit f1 of keys1 and f2 of keys2. If keys1 is empty: when keys2 is non-empty it writes release events (make = 0) for the keys in keys2 to vkbd and ukbd and clears keys2; return 0. If keys2 is empty (and keys1 is not): it copies keys1 into keys2, writes press events (make = 1) for the keys in keys1 and clears keys1; return 0. If both are non-empty: it builds a diff bitmap of keys that were in keys2 but are not in keys1 (clearing them from keys2), then, for each key in keys1, sets it in keys2 if it was not there (a new press, kept in keys1) or clears it from keys1 if it was already pressed. It writes release events for the diff keys when the first diff bit index is greater than 0, and press events for the remaining keys1 bits (and then clears keys1) when the first remaining bit index is greater than 0; a key with bit index 0 therefore produces no event in this branch, and keys1 is not cleared if only bit 0 remains. Afterwards keys2 holds exactly the currently pressed keys (it is not a union with the released ones, which were removed). Nothing is allocated; the diff bitmap is a local.

name: bnep_recv_setup_connection_req
prose: Handles a BNEP setup-connection request (static, usr.sbin/bluetooth/btpand/bnep.c:303-375). It returns 0 (consuming nothing) if size < 1, or, after reading the length byte len, if size < len * 2 + 1. If the channel state is neither CHANNEL_WAIT_CONNECT_REQ nor CHANNEL_OPEN it logs 'ignored' and returns len * 2 + 1 without sending a response or changing the state. Otherwise len must be 2, 4 or 16 (else the response code is BNEP_SETUP_INVALID_UUID_SIZE); the destination UUID is compared with the NAP, GN and PANU UUIDs (offset 2 for 16-bit UUIDs) and its class must equal the global service_class, else the code is BNEP_SETUP_INVALID_DST_UUID. The source UUID is then compared with the same three UUIDs; the response is BNEP_SETUP_INVALID_SRC_UUID when the source matches none (src == 0) or when neither the destination nor the source is PANU (the source is not compared with service_class). If all checks pass the response is BNEP_SETUP_SUCCESS, the channel state becomes CHANNEL_OPEN and channel_timeout(chan, 0) is called. In every case after the state check (success or any error code) it sends a BNEP_SETUP_CONNECTION_RESPONSE control message with that code via bnep_send_control and returns len * 2 + 1. The state is changed only on success.

name: __event_dispatch
prose: Runs one round of the btpand event loop (static, usr.sbin/bluetooth/btpand/event.c:85-209; returns 0 normally, -1 only when select fails). It clears the fd sets, initialises the global current queue (TAILQ_INIT, discarding anything left in it from an earlier round) and sets a default 10 second select timeout. It then drains the pending queue: each event is removed from pending with event_del, its timeout (time left until expire, zero if already expired) lowers the select timeout when smaller, its fd is added to the read and/or write sets according to EV_READ/EV_WRITE (when fd >= 0), and it is appended to current. It calls select; if select returns a negative value it returns -1 at that point, with the events still on the current queue and not on pending (they are not re-armed). Otherwise it processes the current queue in order, removing each event from it: if nfd > 0 (the remaining ready count) and the fd is ready in the read or write set, a persistent event is re-added with event_add (with its saved timeout if it had one), nfd is decremented once and the callback is called with the fd and its READ/WRITE flags; a non-persistent ready event is not re-added. If the event was not dispatched that way (not ready, or nfd had already reached 0): an event without a timeout is re-added with no timeout; an event whose timeout has expired is re-added first if persistent and then its callback is called (non-persistent ones are not re-added); an event whose timeout has not expired is re-linked into pending. Because nfd is decremented once per dispatched event, several events sharing a ready fd can exhaust the count so that some are not dispatched in this round. It then returns 0, and the current queue is empty after a successful round. Callbacks may add or delete events. The callers (event_dispatch) loop on a 0 result.

prose: Real name child_leader_run (usr.sbin/bsdinstall/runconsoles/child.c:220-386; the slice 263-386 is its tail). If new_session is true it calls setsid (err(EX_OSERR) on failure), otherwise it puts itself in a new process group with setpgid (err(EX_OSERR) on failure). In the leader it records grandchild_pid, registers kill_wait_all_descendants_err_exit as the exit hook, restores the signal mask, signals the start-grandchild barrier and waits via wait_grandchild_descendants. If the grandchild was killed by a signal it re-raises that signal death via reproduce_signal_death; if it exited normally it calls exit with its status; otherwise exit(EXIT_FAILURE).

name: camdd_worker
prose: Thread body for one camdd device (usr.sbin/camdd/camdd.c:1676-1878; arg is the struct camdd_dev). It locks dev->mutex, sets CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_ACTIVE and loops. In each pass, for a reading device (write_dev == 0) it computes the queue depths and byte counts and calls camdd_queue(dev, NULL) while either the combined queue depths are below the combined target depths or the queued bytes (ours plus the peer's) are below three times the peer's block size; a return of 1 ends the queuing, any other nonzero return sets error_exit and goes to bailout. If the run queue is non-empty it calls dev->run while the target queue depth exceeds cur_active_io (-1 sets CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_EOF and error_exit and stops, another nonzero value just stops). If CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_EOF or PEER_EOF is set: a writer exits when its work queue is empty, num_run_queue is 0 and cur_active_io is 0; a reader exits immediately when PEER_EOF is set (without draining), else when EOF is set and the peer work and done queues, active I/O and run queue are all empty. Otherwise it waits in kevent (with the device mutex released) using a zero timeout for a reader with no active I/O and fewer queued peer bytes than the peer block size, and no timeout otherwise; a kevent error warns and goes to bailout; EVFILT_READ calls dev->fetch if set (-1 sets error_exit and exits), EVFILT_SIGNAL exits on SIGINT, EVFILT_USER feeds work_queue buffers to camdd_queue (-1 sets error_exit and exits) and passes peer_done_queue buffers to camdd_peer_done, and an unknown filter just warns. At bailout it clears CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_ACTIVE, unlocks the mutex, sets need_exit, posts camdd_sem and returns NULL; resources are not cleaned up here.

name: dep_setup
prose: Builds the jail dependency graph (usr.sbin/jail/state.c:54-149). If docf is 0 (no config file) it looks only at the first jail on cfjails: for each name in its IP_DEPEND parameter, if running_jail(name, 0) returns NULL it prints 'depends on nonexistent jail' with warnx and marks that jail JF_FAILED; it then returns without building dependency lists or detecting loops. Otherwise it counts the jails, builds jails_byname (emalloc) and sorts it with qsort, then for each jail that is not already failed: every IP_DEPEND value is looked up with find_jail and, if found, added with dep_add (counting deps), else it prints 'depends on undefined jail' and marks the jail JF_FAILED; and if the jail name contains a '.', the part of the name before its last '.' is looked up and, if that jail exists, a DF_LIGHT dependency is added (counting ldeps). A loop check runs only if there was at least one dependency and either more than one dependency or at least one light dependency (deps && (deps > 1 || ldeps)): it calls start_state(NULL, 0, 0, 0), moves jails off the ready queue back to cfjails calling dep_done(j, DF_NOFAIL), and every jail still left on the depend queue is reported with 'dependency loop' and marked JF_FAILED (then released the same way); finally it clears DF_SEEN on every dependency edge. The temporary name buffer is freed. It returns nothing. The jails_byname array is not freed here.

name: dep_done
prose: Releases the jails that waited on j (usr.sbin/jail/state.c:231-261). It chooses the direction: for a stopping jail (JF_DO_STOP) the edges are followed in the opposite sense. For each dependency edge of j in that list it skips the edge, without marking it, if it is already marked DF_SEEN or if flags contains DF_LIGHT but the edge does not. For each remaining edge it sets DF_SEEN and takes the other jail dj; if flags does not contain DF_NOFAIL, j has JF_FAILED set, and the combination of j's operation bits and JF_DEPEND is not exactly (JF_SET | JF_DEPEND) (the test masks j->flags with JF_OP_MASK | JF_DEPEND), then dj is marked JF_FAILED, with a 'skipped' warning printed first when dj was not already JF_DEPEND or JF_FAILED and verbose >= 0. It then decrements dj->ndeps, and if that reaches zero while dj is on the depend queue, dj is requeued on the ready queue. It returns nothing.

name: lockchk
prose: Checks whether the printer lock file slockf names a live daemon and records its current job (usr.sbin/lpr/common_source/rmjob.c:147-179). It does PRIV_START and fopen(slockf, "r"). If the open fails with EACCES it calls fatal(pp, ...) (no return); if it fails for another reason it returns 0 directly, without the matching PRIV_END. After a successful open it calls PRIV_END, reads the first line into the global line with get_line (none: close, return 0), and sets the global cur_daemon = atoi(line), which is done before the liveness test and so also changes cur_daemon on the following return 0. If kill(cur_daemon, 0) fails with an errno other than EPERM the file is closed and it returns 0. Otherwise it freads the rest of the file into current, retrying with sleep(i) up to five times while fread returns <= 0 (after the retries it sets n = 1, so current becomes the empty string); then it NUL-terminates current at index n - 1 (overwriting the last byte read, normally a newline), closes the file and returns 1.

name: main
prose: Entry point of mountd (usr.sbin/mountd/mountd.c:420-808; slice cut the head). It tries pidfile_open: if another mountd holds the pid file (EEXIST) it calls errx(1, ...); any other failure only warns. It parses options (-2, -A, -a, -d, -e, -h host (strdup'ed host list), -l, -N, -n, -p port (a non-numeric, zero or too large port calls usage(); the string is kept in svcport_str), -R (disables rpcbind), -r, -S, -s); an unknown option calls usage(). It warns if -s was given without -h, and if the nfsd kernel module is not present it tries kldload, calling errx(1, "NFS server is not available") if that fails. It records the export file names, reads the export list and mount list, daemonises unless debugging or -n, installs signal handlers and writes the pid file. When rpcbind is enabled it unregisters the mount program versions, sets the maximum record size, sets the privileged-port sysctl (a failure other than ENOENT is logged and exit(1)), and creates the services: it walks the netconfig entries, creating sockets per address and port with bind retries (several allocation failures and bind failures end with exit(1)), then frees sock_fd and the port_list entries and array before the service loop (the host list and any svcport_str are kept), and exit(1)s if no service was created (xcreated == 0). It then runs the service loop forever: with rpcbind enabled it select()s on the RPC descriptors and calls svc_getreqset (a select failure other than EINTR is logged and exit(1)), otherwise it sigsuspend()s; SIGHUP reloads the export list but not more often than the reload delay. The function does not return. Only the head, the option handling and the exit points were read; the socket-creation loop (lines 648-735) was only skimmed.

name: r_protocol
prose: Real name r_protocol (static, usr.sbin/moused/msconvd/msconvd.c:1291-1822; the packet called it mouse_packet_parser). It decodes one byte rBuf from the mouse device into the mousestatus act. For the KIDSPAD and GTCO_DIGIPAD protocols it returns the result of kidspad() or gtco_digipad() directly. Otherwise it uses static state (a packet buffer pBuf of 8 bytes with index pBufP, previous x/y and a VersaPad flag) and the protocol description table cur_proto. If a packet is in progress and the byte fails the per-protocol continuation test (non-PS/2 only) or is 0x80, the partial packet is dropped (pBufP = 0). If no packet is in progress and the byte does not look like a header byte it returns 0. If pBufP has reached the packet length and the byte is not a header, it is treated as an optional extra byte after a full packet: a byte failing the extra-byte test clears pBufP and returns 0, otherwise the protocol-specific handling (such as the MouseMan fourth byte for the middle button, or JogDial/IntelliMouse extra data) updates dz and the buttons, then act->flags is set (MOUSE_POSCHANGED if dx, dy or dz is non-zero, ORed with obutton ^ button), pBufP is reset and act->flags is returned. A header byte after a full packet restarts the buffer. The byte is stored in pBuf and the function returns 0 until the packet length is reached. On a full packet it clears dz, saves the old button state in obutton and decodes by protocol (Microsoft/MouseMan/X10, GlidePoint, ThinkingMouse, IntelliMouse, MouseSystems, JogDial, HitTablet, MM Series, Logitech, VersaPad, PS/2 variants including model-specific cases, sysmouse), where an X10 MouseRemote button packet is forwarded to rodent.mremcfd (when >= 0) and returns 0; an unknown protocol returns 0 (the final switch has a default returning 0). It does not reset pBufP after a full packet because an extra byte may follow, and returns act->flags computed as above. Partly read: the per-protocol decoding cases between lines 1534 and 1805 were only skimmed.

name: mpt_lock_volume
prose: Locks a RAID volume by opening its device node read-write (usr.sbin/mptutil/mpt_config.c:90-117; the opened descriptor is deliberately leaked, see the comment at lines 85-89). It calls mpt_query_disk(VolumeBus, VolumeID, &qd) to find the volume's device name. If that returns ENOENT (no CAM device for the volume, treated as already locked) it returns 0 without opening anything. If it returns any other nonzero error it prints 'Unable to lookup volume device name' with warnc and returns that error. Otherwise it builds _PATH_DEV plus the device name and open()s it O_RDWR; on failure it saves errno, warns 'Unable to lock volume <name>' and returns that errno; on success it returns 0. The file descriptor from a successful open is never closed or returned, so it stays open until the process exits. It touches OS state (device nodes) and uses mpt_query_disk, so no formal contract is given.

name: process_cmd
prose: Executes one interactive mtest command line (static, usr.sbin/mtest/mtest.c:375-828). It sets line to the text after the command letter (skipping blanks after cmd[1]; it reads cmd[1] even if the line has only one character) and switches on *cmd. '?' calls usage(). 'q' closes s and calls exit(0); it never returns. 's' reads an integer n >= 1 (else prints -1), sleeps n seconds and prints ok. 'j' and 'l' (join and leave) parse interface and group arguments; a parse or lookup failure prints -1; otherwise they call setsockopt on the IPv4 socket s or IPv6 socket s6; when the needed socket is negative they warn EPROTONOSUPPORT and fall through to print -1; a setsockopt failure warns and also falls through to -1; success prints ok. 'i' and 'e' parse 'ifname group n' (bad parse or n out of range prints -1), and if the address family has no usable socket they only warn and print nothing; they then read n further address lines with fgets from fp (the fp parameter is marked __unused but is used), resolve each with getaddrinfo (failure prints -1) and call setsourcefilter, printing ok or warning and printing nothing on failure. 't' and 'b' (allow or block a source) read the current source filter with getsourcefilter (an unsupported family or a getsourcefilter failure only warns) and then call setsockopt, printing ok on success and -1 for parse or lookup failures, and only a warning for setsockopt failure. 'g' prints the filter mode, the source count and each source, then ok, or -1 when the arguments do not parse or getsourcefilter fails. 'a' and 'd' add or delete a link-layer multicast address with SIOCADDMULTI/SIOCDELMULTI on s, warning (and printing nothing) on parse errors and printing -1 on ioctl failure or ok on success. 'm' prints a warning and -1. 'p' reads an interface name and flag, gets and sets IFF_PPROMISC through SIOCGIFFLAGS/SIOCSIFFLAGS, and prints 'changed to 0x...' or only warns on ioctl failure, printing -1 if the arguments do not parse. A newline does nothing and any other command prints 'invalid command'. It returns nothing. Details of the 'j', 'l', 't', 'b' and 'g' branches were read only in outline.
